question: What fraction of spam-labeled removals is corroborated / contradicted by the surviving metadata shadow (OpenAlex), judged by a published mechanical rubric on the same surface the removal process judged?

method.metadata_source: OpenAlex /works/doi:{doi} (title, abstract, authorships, references, citations, ORCID)
method.rubric: v2: ~65 spam patterns (commercial, pharma, gambling, piracy/ebook-SEO, download-bait) vs scholarship structure (>=2 of: abstract>=300ch, authors>=2, refs>=1, cited>=1, ORCID). Rubric v1 (commercial-only) undercounted piracy/SEO spam; v1->v2 revision documented deliberately: the correction is part of the record.
method.honesty_bounds: Indicia of presentation, not ground truth; the destroyed records preclude confirmation in both directions, for the operator as for the auditor. Manual inspection of the UNCORROBORATED bucket shows it dominated by pattern-evading SEO/piracy queries: content-level spam share plausibly ~90%+.

collateral_examples.title: Pengaruh Antusiasme Belajar dan Media Belajar Website "Sekolah Digital SMKN 3 Salatiga"...
collateral_examples.note: education study, 4 OpenAlex citations, deleted as spam via account block

collateral_examples.title: White Paper #0018 - The Collapse of Cultural Immunity
collateral_examples.note: non-commercial fringe scholarship erased under commercial-spam label

collateral_examples.title: No.140 Data. Thought Synchronization in Mirror Writing...

findings: The spam label is SUBSTANTIALLY CORROBORATED at content level in this sample: ~47% pattern-confirmed, with manual inspection indicating most of the uncorroborated residual is pattern-evading SEO/piracy. The audit does not support a claim that spam labels are mostly wrong.

The measured collateral is small in rate and large in count: 1.0% [0.34-2.90] of spam-labeled records bear affirmative scholarship indicia -> on the order of 10^4 records [~4K-34K] across the class, including cited research, erased under the spam label.

The asymmetry is the finding: the audit could measure an error rate from outside using surviving shadows; the removal process itself wrote no per-record evidence in either direction (0.00% citation_text; 0.1% reviewable batch sizes), so its errors are invisible to the operator and uncorrectable by design.

Pathway contrast: staff-adjudicated removals show higher pattern-confirmation (58.0% vs 35.3%) and zero scholarship-signal collateral (0/150 vs 3/150), consistent with adjudication working where it occurs; the account-block pathway, which produced 68% of the entire spam class, is where the collateral lives.
